$comment: Generated from repository.yaml by `uv run dd-gen-schema <path to repository.yaml>`. Do not edit.

Affiliation.description: The researcher's institution, matched against the institutions a registry lists.
Affiliation.title: Affiliation

ChosenRepository.description: The repository a researcher chose to deposit the project's data in, from the shortlist, by the identifier of the registry that lists it: the conductor fills it into a Message, and into the input of an agent that mixes in GivenProjectRepository, so that the agent knows a repository is chosen and which (docs/specs/projects.md). The last choice stands until a researcher chooses again.

chosen_repository_name.description: The chosen repository's name, as the pinned re3data export gives it.

chosen_repository_id.description: The chosen repository's identifier: its re3data identifier, such as r3d100010468, where re3data lists it, else its DataCite repository identifier, such as bl.york. The conductor always gives it; a caller that sends only chosen_re3data_id has it given from that.

chosen_re3data_id.description: The chosen repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010468, where it has one.

ChosenRepository.title: ChosenRepository

FactKind.description: What a project fact is about (docs/specs/projects.md).
FactKind.title: FactKind

FileDecision.description: Whether a file of the inventory is to be deposited.
FileDecision.title: FileDecision

InstitutionRepository.description: One repository the deployment's profile names as its institution's (the profile's institution_repositories, docs/specs/policy-and-identity.md). It names a registry's record by repository_id and adds only what the deployment vouches for that no registry holds: the conductor fills it into the input of an agent that mixes in GivenInstitutionRepositories.

repository_id.description: A repository's identifier in the registry that lists it: its re3data identifier, such as r3d100012124, where re3data lists it, else its DataCite repository identifier, such as bl.york. An override names it in place of re3data_id for a repository re3data does not list.

profile_ref.description: The reference of the profile that vouches for the facts, as profile:<id>@v<version>; an agent cites them under it.

institution_name.description: The institution whose repository it is, where the registry names another operator, such as a consortium or a platform.

institution_ror.description: That institution's ROR identifier, as a URL.

data_access_types.description: The access the repository offers, as re3data names it (open, embargoed, restricted, closed).

data_licences.description: The licences the repository offers for data, as SPDX identifiers or URLs.

charges_deposit_fee.description: Whether the repository charges a fee to deposit. Unlike re3data, a deployment may say it charges none.

guidance.description: The pages the deployment checked the facts it vouches for against.

InstitutionRepository.title: InstitutionRepository

LocationPrecision.description: The precision at which a location may be published.
LocationPrecision.title: LocationPrecision

ProjectFact.description: One fact about a project that a check agent proposes and a person confirms: a funder, a repository a funder or institution requires, whether a file is deposited, whether a sensitive field or file may be published and at what precision, the licence, an output a data management plan committed to share, a standard, vocabulary or format the researcher chose for the dataset, or which attached document is the project's data management plan (docs/specs/projects.md). fact_kind says which of the value slots apply; fact_subject is the key a person's decision counts by, so the last decision on a subject stands. An agent's payload carries proposals in proposed_facts; only a person's decision makes one a fact, and the conductor gives the facts a person decided to every drafter and orchestrator in the project as project_decisions, without proposed_because.

fact_kind.description: What the fact is about, which says which value slots apply.

fact_subject.description: The key a decision counts by within its kind: the funder's identifier or name, the repository's re3data identifier or name, the file's path, the field or path judged sensitive, licence, or the standard chosen and what it is chosen for. The last decision on a kind and subject stands.

fact_funder_name.description: The funder's name, as its policy record or the researcher gives it.

fact_funder_ror.description: The funder's ROR identifier, as a URL, where it is known.

fact_crossref_funder_id.description: The funder's Crossref Funder ID, as a DOI URL, where it is known.

fact_re3data_id.description: The required repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010199, where known.

fact_required_by.description: The funders, journals or institutions that require the repository.

fact_file_path.description: The path of the file the fact is about, relative to the dataset's root folder, as the inventory gives it.

file_decision.description: Whether the file is to be deposited.

fact_check_kind.description: The kind of check that raised the fact, in the checking agent's words, such as duplicate, system_file or third_party. Kept as it was given; the core does not enumerate it.

sensitive_subject.description: The field name, or the file path, judged sensitive, such as a lat or lon field, or a file of site coordinates.

sensitivity_decision.description: Whether the sensitive field or file may be published, and how.

location_precision.description: For a location that may be published or generalised, the precision agreed. Absent where the subject is not a location.

licence_id.description: The licence decided, as an SPDX identifier or a URL.

commitment_repository.description: For a sharing commitment, the repository the plan committed to share the output in, as the plan names it; absent where it names none. A plan that names several for one output gives a sharing commitment for each.

commitment_access.description: For a sharing commitment, how openly the plan committed to share the output (such as open, embargoed or on request), as the plan says it; absent where it says nothing.

commitment_licence.description: For a sharing commitment, the licence the plan committed to, as the plan names it; absent where it names none.

commitment_quote.description: For a sharing commitment, the plan's own words the commitment was read from, verbatim, so the person deciding can see the passage it rests on.

commitment_document.description: For a sharing commitment, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) the quote is from.

standard_name.description: For a standard fact, the name of the standard, vocabulary, ontology or format chosen, as its registry record or the researcher gives it.

standard_id.description: For a standard fact, a persistent identifier of the standard, as a URL, such as its FAIRsharing DOI, where it is known.

standard_kind.description: For a standard fact, what kind of standard was chosen, where it is known.

standard_target.description: For a standard fact, what the standard is chosen for: dataset, or field:<name> for one field of the dataset's tables. Absent means the dataset.

plan_document.description: For a data management plan fact, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) that is the project's plan.

proposed_because.description: Why the agent proposes the fact, in a sentence for the person deciding. Kept with the proposal and shown to the person, never given to an agent.

ProjectFact.title: ProjectFact

RepositoryRef.description: A repository named by a funder, journal or institutional policy, or by the researcher. The re3data identifier is used when given; otherwise the name is looked up.

repository_id.description: A repository's identifier in the registry that lists it: its re3data identifier, such as r3d100012124, where re3data lists it, else its DataCite repository identifier, such as bl.york. An override names it in place of re3data_id for a repository re3data does not list.

RepositoryRef.title: RepositoryRef

SensitivityDecision.description: Whether a sensitive field or file may be published.
SensitivityDecision.title: SensitivityDecision

StandardKind.description: What kind of standard a standard fact names.
StandardKind.title: StandardKind

description: What a dataset needs of a repository. With mandated repositories, the agent describes them; with none, it shortlists. Repositories the researcher asked about are described either way, alongside the shortlist when there is one. The mandate and the access constraint come from Phase 2 (governance), usually by way of the orchestrator. In a project the conductor also gives the facts people decided and the repository the researcher chose: a decided required repository is described as mandated, a repository that a confirmed sharing commitment of the data management plan names is described alongside the shortlist (never as mandated), and the chosen one is described when nothing else is asked.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

themes.description: The dataset's discipline, as the broad field of study (e.g. environmental science), and any narrower subjects as further themes. A narrow topic alone (e.g. moorland) may match no repository of the discipline.

data_kinds.description: What the data is, each in one to three words, e.g. interview transcripts, survey microdata or time series. A repository matches a kind only if its record has every word, so a long description (e.g. environmental data logger time series) matches none.

access.description: How the data may be accessed once deposited, as decided in Phase 2. Unset means not yet decided, and no access need is checked.

mandated.description: Only repositories that a funder, journal or institutional policy requires: as a policy result found them in Phase 2, or as the researcher states such a policy requires them. A repository the researcher merely names, prefers or asks about belongs in asked_about. Naming an institution, or being funded by a funder, does not make its repository mandated. A mandated repository replaces the shortlist.

asked_about.description: Repositories the researcher named or asked about (e.g. "what about Zenodo?") that no policy is known to require. Each is described with the needs it meets and misses, alongside the shortlist rather than instead of it.

affiliation.description: The researcher's institution. Its repositories are offered as a fallback, after those of the dataset's discipline and before generalist ones, and none is removed, so give the themes as if it were not set.

country.description: The country of the researcher's institution, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code (e.g. GBR), as re3data writes it. A repository that already matches ranks a little higher when operated in this country; it adds no repository to the shortlist on its own. Unset, it is the country re3data records for the affiliation's institution, where re3data lists one.

project_decisions.description: The facts a person in the project decided (ProjectFact), the last decision on each subject, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project decided any. A drafter treats each as supplied.

project_repository.description: The repository a researcher in the project chose last, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project has chosen one.

institution_repositories.description: The repositories the deployment's profile names as its institution's, filled by the conductor from the profile and never by the caller. Absent when the profile names none.
